The core insight is that tournament format influences not only qualification likelihood but also the strategic incentives for teams to score more goals. The four-parameter pot-based Poisson model captures team strength via discrete tiers, simulating match outcomes under both old and new formats. By computing the marginal gain in qualification or elimination-avoidance probability from an extra goal, we derive the attacking incentive metric. This metric reveals that the new 36-team incomplete round-robin increases attacking incentives by 119% for direct R16 qualification and 58% for avoiding elimination. These findings suggest that structural changes in fixture design can significantly alter expected goal dynamics, necessitating format-aware adjustments in GSE’s goal-supremacy models. The model's validity hinges on its ability to replicate real-world goal outcomes under varying incentives—a testable condition for empirical validation.
